evidence: batch_0037, 120 games with five personalities drawn per game: sieger 86.5% [74.7, 93.3] against brawler 21.2% [12.2, 34.0], intervals nowhere near overlapping. A policy that groups and hunts kills loses four games in five to one that ignores it and hits towers.
hypothesis: Fighting is mispriced, not merely unrewarded. A kill pays 1 AP and a few rounds of the victim's cooldown; a tower pays 11 chips, which is 11 AP, and moves the win condition. Tripling what a kill pays and lengthening the window it opens should make the fight worth having without touching what the map is for.
success_metric: In a personality batch: the brawler clears 35% and the spread between the best and worst personality falls below 40 points, from 65.
revert_if: Median game length leaves 13-16 rounds, or any personality clears 80%, or champion kills per game more than double (a kill snowball is not the goal).
side_effects: Longer death timers mean a killed champion misses more of the game, which is a pacing lever as well as an economy one - games may shorten. Kills feeding AP couples combat to the shop, so item timings move. The warder and brawler should gain most; the sieger should lose least, since it was never fighting.
note: The two map-shaped levers - pricing objectives higher, or making towers need a wave present - are pillar-adjacent and were left alone for the lead designer.
